content.title: About
content.content: Margarine stick is a vegetable-based spread made from refined plant oils, emulsified with water, salt and flavorings. It is sold in convenient stick form that can be easily sliced and used in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Margarine was first created in the 19th century as a cheaper alternative to butter.
Most modern margarines are fortified with vitamins A and D.
Stick format allows precise portion control and easy handling.
Some brands add plant sterols that may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of plant fats
items.content: Margarine contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids, which can be beneficial for cardiovascular health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Vitamin‑enriched
items.content: Added vitamins A and D support vision, immune function and bone health.

items.title: Low trans‑fat content
items.content: Current production methods keep trans‑fat levels minimal, making it safer than early versions of margarine.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Like any fat, margarine is calorie‑dense, so portion control is important, especially on weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Allergy to plant oils
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to soy or sunflower oil, common ingredients in margarine.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Margarine often contains added salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The stick can be sliced thinly for spreading on bread, used in baking, sautéing, or incorporated into sauces. It melts easily and adds tenderness to doughs and batters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the margarine in the refrigerator at 0 °C to 5 °C, in its original packaging or an airtight container. For long‑term storage it can be frozen at –18 °C.
